source.title: Soft and elastic hydrogel-based microelectronics for localized low-voltage neuromodulation

material: Micropatterned ECH (MECH) elastronic electrode array encapsulated in PFPE-DMA

processing.evidence: UV exposure (Quintel Q4000, Hg Lamp, 350–450nm) at 10mWcm−2 for 20 s was used to crosslink PFPE-DMA

swelling_ratio.evidence: with a swelling ratio of 2.1 when sandwiched by the elastic PFPE-DMA

description.evidence: the MECH microelectrodes showed stable impedance when soaked in PBS for 19 days

duration_days.evidence: the MECH microelectrodes showed stable impedance when soaked in PBS for 19 days

other_outcomes.evidence: Our MECH electrode stimulated leg response at an ultralow voltage of 50mV, without the need to remove or penetrate the epineurium layer
other_outcomes.name: leg stimulation threshold voltage on sciatic nerve

other_outcomes.evidence: implanted the freestanding thin-film device (100μm in thickness) by wrapping it around the sciatic nerve of mice and leaving it inside the freely moving mice for 6 weeks
other_outcomes.name: chronic implantation duration around sciatic nerve

notes: Areal capacitance 9,800 µF cm−2; current density 1,359 mA cm−2 at 0.5 V, 50 Hz in DMEM. No significant change in neurofilament/S-100 vs sham; inflammatory ED1 area comparable to sham. Impedance at 1 kHz of insulated electrodes >100 MΩ.
